(d) equality holds in (c) if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent;
in particular the Robertson bound (b) follows from (c) because the first
square is nonnegative;

(e) if $A$ and $B$ are bounded everywhere-defined self-adjoint operators, then
the product-domain hypothesis $u\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$ holds for every unit
$u\in H$ and clauses (a)-(d) apply to every unit $u$.

No energy-time inequality and no apparatus statement is made.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in the first argument
([[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]]), let $A,B$ be symmetric
densely defined operators on $H$
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]]), and let $u\in D(A)\cap D(B)$
with $\|u\|=1$ satisfy in addition $u\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$, that is
$Bu\in D(A)$ and $Au\in D(B)$. Put
$$a:=\langle Au,u\rangle,\qquad b:=\langle Bu,u\rangle,\qquad x:=(A-a)u,\qquad y:=(B-b)u,\qquad \Delta A:=\|x\|,\qquad \Delta B:=\|y\|,$$
and write $\{A,B\}u:=ABu+BAu$ and $[A,B]u:=ABu-BAu$ for the pairings at $u$.
Then:

(a) $a,b\in\mathbb R$, $x,y\in H$, and
$$\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle=\tfrac12\bigl\langle\{(A-a),(B-b)\}u,u\bigr\rangle=\tfrac12\langle\{A,B\}u,u\rangle-ab, \qquad \langle[A,B]u,u\rangle=-2i\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle ;$$

(b) *(Robertson bound)* $\Delta A\,\Delta B\ge\tfrac12\bigl|\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle\bigr|$;

(c) *(Schroedinger-Robertson bound)*
$$(\Delta A)^{2}(\Delta B)^{2}\ge\Bigl(\tfrac12\bigl\langle\{(A-a),(B-b)\}u,u\bigr\rangle\Bigr)^{2}+\tfrac14\bigl|\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle\bigr|^{2},$$
that is, with the expanded anticommutator pairing
$(\Delta A)^{2}(\Delta B)^{2}\ge\bigl(\tfrac12\langle\{A,B\}u,u\rangle-ab\bigr)^{2}+\tfrac14\bigl|\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle\bigr|^{2}$;

(d) equality holds in (c) if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent;
in particular the Robertson bound (b) follows from (c) because the first
square is nonnegative;

(e) if $A$ and $B$ are bounded everywhere-defined self-adjoint operators, then
the product-domain hypothesis $u\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$ holds for every unit
$u\in H$ and clauses (a)-(d) apply to every unit $u$.

No energy-time inequality and no apparatus statement is made.

**(a) Dimensions.** Write $\ell$, $\tau$, $\mu$, $\vartheta$ for the four independent dimension symbols of length, duration, mass and electric charge. A **dimension** is an element of $\mathbb Q^{4}$, written $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ with $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb Q$; products and inverses of dimensions are componentwise addition and negation, and the dimensionless dimension $\ell^{0}\tau^{0}\mu^{0}\vartheta^{0}$ is abbreviated $1$. The conventions assign to each quantity of the framework a dimension $[X]$, subject to $[XY]=[X][Y]$, $[X/Y]=[X][Y]^{-1}$ and $[dX/du]=[X][u]^{-1}$, with sums meaningful only between quantities of equal dimension, in which case the sum carries that dimension. For a rational power $q$, dimension powers mean $[X]^q=\ell^{qa}\tau^{qb}\mu^{qc}\vartheta^{qd}$ when $[X]=\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$. Rational exponents include the half-integer wave-function dimensions in clause (d); the integer-exponent dimensions form the subgroup $\mathbb Z^4$. These are consistency requirements on the conventions, not laws of nature.

For extensions using temperature, adjoin an independent dimension symbol $\Theta$: the enlarged group is $\mathbb Q^4\times\mathbb Q$, written $\ell^a\tau^b\mu^c\vartheta^d\Theta^e$, with the same componentwise rules. The preceding group embeds by $e=0$, so all previously assigned dimensions are preserved. Temperature has dimension $\Theta$, the Boltzmann constant has dimension $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-2}\Theta^{-1}$, and entropy in joules per kelvin has that same dimension; a dimensionless entropy remains dimensionless. This convention does not assign a temperature or an entropy to any system.

**(b) Reference units.** The **metre** (m), **second** (s), **kilogram** (kg) and **coulomb** (C) are the reference units of length, duration, mass and charge; a quantity of dimension $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ is expressed in the unit $\mathrm m^{a}\mathrm s^{b}\mathrm kg^{c}\mathrm C^{d}$. Coordinates of an inertial frame are read with the time coordinate $t$ in seconds, $[t]=\tau$, and the spatial coordinates $x_{i}$ in metres, $[x_{i}]=\ell$; slice distances of the arena are read in metres. In the temperature extension the reference unit of $\Theta$ is the kelvin (K), so the general reference unit gains a factor $\mathrm K^e$.

**(c) Defining constants of the current SI.** The framework keeps $\hbar$ explicit. In the current SI the constants $h$, $c$ and $e$ are exact defining constants, with the values $h=6{,}626\,070\,15\times10^{-34}$ J s, $c=2{,}99792458\times10^{8}$ m s$^{-1}$ and $e=1{,}602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}$ C, and $\hbar:=h/(2\pi)$. These are real scalar constants with dimensions and units $[h]=[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$ (J s), $[c]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ (m s$^{-1}$), and $[e]=\vartheta$ (C). The vacuum permeability $\mu_{0}$ is a positive real scalar that is experimentally determined in the current SI, with $[\mu_{0}]=\mu\ell\vartheta^{-2}$ (N A$^{-2}$ = H m$^{-1}$); $\varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1}$ is a positive real scalar with $[\varepsilon_{0}]=\mu^{-1}\ell^{-3}\tau^{2}\vartheta^{2}$ (F m$^{-1}$). These are unit-convention statements of the SI, not measurements reported by this framework; $c$ enters the framework only through the separate radiation assumptions adopted on their own pages, not in the nonrelativistic spacetime of [[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]].

**(d) Dimensions and types of the framework's quantities.** The dimension map is fixed on the following quantities.

1. State quantities: a position wave function of a system with $d$ spatial dimensions and $r$ internal components is an almost-everywhere equivalence class in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with dimension $\ell^{-d/2}$, its norm $\|\psi\|$ is dimensionless, and an abstract normalized state and the density operators of the state postulate are dimensionless.
2. Probability: the outcome probability $\mu(B)$ of the observable postulate is a dimensionless number; a position density $|\psi|^{2}$ has dimension $\ell^{-d}$; a momentum wave function normalized against $\mathrm d^{d}p$ has dimension $(\mu\ell\tau^{-1})^{-d/2}$; an amplitude for a finite outcome is a dimensionless complex number, while an amplitude read against a detector coordinate carries the square-root of the inverse of the detector measure.
3. Frame parameters ([[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]]): $[b]=\tau$, $[a_{i}]=\ell$, $[v_{i}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $[R_{ij}]=1$.
4. Mechanical quantities: action $[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; energy and the Hamiltonian eigenvalues $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$; momentum $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$; position components $\ell$; angular momentum and spin $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; mass $\mu$; velocity of a free spinless model $\ell\tau^{-1}$; force $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$; a real potential energy $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$.
5. Probability current: in the ordinary continuous-field regime, fix an integer $d\ge1$, an open spatial region $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ and an open time interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$. A **probability current density** is a declared continuous map $j:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^d$, whose spatial components have dimension $\ell^{1-d}\tau^{-1}$ and reference unit $\mathrm m^{1-d}\mathrm s^{-1}$. At fixed time it is a spatial vector field; its signed normal component is read as probability transported per unit spatial $(d-1)$-area and time. Explicitly, for a flat face $S=\{x:x_k=a,\ a_i\le x_i\le b_i\ (i\ne k)\}\subset\Omega$, with $a_i<b_i$ and chosen normal $n=\epsilon e_k$, $\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}$, define its **signed probability flux** at $t\in I$ as $\Phi_S(t):=\epsilon\int_{\prod_{i\ne k}[a_i,b_i]}j_k(x_1,\ldots,x_{k-1},a,x_{k+1},\ldots,x_d,t)\prod_{i\ne k}dx_i$. Here $e_k$ is the $k$th coordinate unit vector and the integral uses $(d-1)$-dimensional Lebesgue measure; for $d=1$ this means $\Phi_{\{a\}}(t)=\epsilon j(a,t)$. The flux has dimension $\tau^{-1}$ and unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$; positive sign means transport in the chosen normal direction. Fluxes through curved surfaces, or currents with weaker regularity, require separately specified surface measures or traces. This fixes the quantity type and flux convention; it supplies neither a current associated to an arbitrary $L^2$ state nor a conservation or detector law. Each dynamical model supplies its current construction and balance hypotheses.
6. Electric quantities of the model parameters: charge has dimension $\vartheta$; a magnetic moment has dimension $\ell^{2}\vartheta\tau^{-1}$, equivalently $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{2}=\mathrm J\,\mathrm T^{-1}$, and a gyromagnetic parameter $\gamma$ in the relation $\boldsymbol\mu=\gamma\mathbf S$ has dimension $\mu^{-1}\vartheta$, equivalently $\mathrm s^{-1}\mathrm T^{-1}$; these quantities appear only in the model assumptions that introduce them.
7. Statistical quantities: a mean has the dimension of its outcome coordinate, a variance the square of it and a standard deviation it; a mean, variance or higher moment exists only when the corresponding moment of the outcome probability is finite, so a symbolic average is not a number unless that integrability is established. Angles and phases are dimensionless under the radian convention.
8. Quantities of later extension assumptions - radiation frequencies and energies, electric dipole moments, cross sections, temperatures and entropies - are declared with their dimensions and units by the items that introduce those assumptions, under the rules fixed here; they are not part of the present list.

**(e) Conventions only.** No numerical value of any model parameter is fixed by this item: no mass, charge, spin label, potential or measured constant is asserted, and natural-unit shorthand (for example setting $\hbar=1$ or $c=1$) is read as an abbreviation for the corresponding SI-dimensioned statement with the constant restored.

**(a) Setting.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the
observable and probability postulate P2 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned sharp observable with
declared unit $u_{A}$ and outcome law $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ in a preparation
$\rho$, in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b).

**(b) Preparation variance.** When the mean
$m(\rho):=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and the second
moment $\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ of the outcome
law are finite, the **preparation variance** of $(A,u_{A})$ in $\rho$ is
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A):=\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\rho)\bigr)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda),$$
read in the square $u_{A}^{2}$ of the declared unit, and the **preparation
spread** is $\Delta_{\rho}A:=\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A)^{1/2}\ge0$, read in
the unit $u_{A}$. When either quantity is not finite the variance and the
spread of the pair in $\rho$ are **not defined**; the definition does not
extend them by $+\infty$.

**(c) Values and hypotheses.** The variance and its hypotheses are exactly
those of the moment theorem: for a pure preparation of a unit vector
$\psi\in D(A)$ the spread is $\Delta_{\psi}A=\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\|$,
equal to $\bigl(\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}\bigr)^{1/2}$
when $\psi\in D(A^{2})$; for a preparation $\rho$ the identities and existence
criteria are those of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] and
[[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]]. In particular, for an orthonormal density expansion
$\rho=\sum_n w_nT_{u_n,u_n}$, the mean is finite exactly when
$$\sum_{n:w_n>0}w_n\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}(\lambda)<\infty,$$
by [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]] clause (d); zero-weight
indices are omitted before evaluating their component integrals. For a pure
unit vector the corresponding criterion is membership in $D(|A|^{1/2})$
by clause (b). Componentwise domain membership alone does not imply
convergence of the weighted sum, and finite moments are not automatic.

**(d) Products of spreads.** For two assigned sharp observables $(A,u_{A})$
and $(B,u_{B})$ in a common preparation $\rho$ in which both spreads are
defined, the product $\Delta_{\rho}A\,\Delta_{\rho}B$ is a nonnegative real
number read in the product unit $u_{A}u_{B}$; for a pure preparation of a unit
vector in $D(A)\cap D(B)$ it is
$\|(A-a)\psi\|\,\|(B-b)\psi\|$ with the real means $a=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$
and $b=\langle B\psi,\psi\rangle$.

**(e) Reading and scope.** The spread $\Delta_{\rho}A$ is a property of the
pair (preparation, assigned observable): it is the standard deviation of the
outcome law that P2 assigns. It is not an apparatus resolution, not a
measurement error and not a disturbance of the preparation; those are further
objects that require a declared instrument or apparatus model and are not
introduced here. Clause (b) makes no claim that a preparation realizes a
specific laboratory state, that a laboratory procedure measures $A$ with
resolution $u_{A}$, or that the spread is observed in any experiment; the
identification of an apparatus with the pair $(A,u_{A})$ is a tested
identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] fixes the units in which the
displays are read.

derivations.claim: [Weak form] Let $\psi\in D(A)\cap D(B)$ be a unit vector. By [F1] the means $a=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $b=\langle B\psi,\psi\rangle$ are real, the spreads $\Delta_{\psi}A$ and $\Delta_{\psi}B$ are defined, and they equal the norms of the centered vectors $x=(A-a)\psi$ and $y=(B-b)\psi$. By [F3], $\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle=\operatorname{Im}\langle A\psi,B\psi\rangle$ and $\Delta_{\psi}A\Delta_{\psi}B\ge|\operatorname{Im}\langle A\psi,B\psi\rangle|$, which is (a).

[Robertson form] Assume in addition $\psi\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$. Then $A,B$ satisfy the product-domain hypothesis of [F2] at $u=\psi$; combining the Robertson bound and the anticommutator refinement of [F2] with the identifications of [F1] gives the two displays of (b), and the equality clause transfers because the centered vectors there are exactly $(A-a)\psi$ and $(B-b)\psi$. The pairing $\langle[A,B]\psi,\psi\rangle$ is purely imaginary by [F2]. This is (b).

[Bounded case] If $A$ and $B$ are bounded everywhere-defined self-adjoint operators, then $D(A)=D(B)=H$ and all products are everywhere defined, so the hypotheses of clauses (a) and (b) hold for every unit $\psi\in H$; clauses (a) and (b) apply verbatim. This is (c).

[Units and scope] The units are those of [F4]; the preparation spread is the outcome-law spread of [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]] and no apparatus, disturbance, joint-law or time quantity enters steps 1.1-2.1, which is the scope statement (d).

boundaries.reason: Two assigned observables and one unit vector are given; no empty family, empty sum or empty index set occurs.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.1 allows $\Delta_{\psi}A=0$: then the pairing $\operatorname{Im}\langle A\psi,B\psi\rangle$ vanishes by [F2] and the weak bound reads $0\ge0$.
Step 3.1 covers the bounded case for every pair, including $A=B$; steps 1.1 and 2.1 are uniform in the pair.
Steps 1.1 and 2.1 include vanishing centered vectors, and step 2.1 imports the linear-dependence equality clause covering that degenerate case.

boundaries.reason: No interval endpoint or limit at infinity is asserted; all pairings are finite under the stated domain hypotheses.
Only the choice hypotheses carried by the cited spectral reading are assumed; no selection of representatives occurs.

boundaries.evidence: Step 2.1 states that linear dependence of the centered vectors gives equality in the refined bound.
Step 2.1 also records that equality in the refined bound forces the centered vectors to be linearly dependent.

risk_review.notes: All four steps checked against exact moment/variance suppliers, preparation-spread definition, weak Robertson and anticommutator bound. Means/spreads finite at unit vectors in D(A) cap D(B); weak form does not call product-domain theorem as load-bearing input because weak-form supplier clause(a) supplies it. Strong form checks both products; commutator sign is -2i Im and purely imaginary. Equality iff centered-vector dependence includes zero variance. Bounded operators supply automatic domains. Units multiply correctly and no apparatus/time/data conclusions enter. Current carrier matches post-reader hash; touched change accepted on current mathematical review.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the
cited scalar operator and spectral suppliers. Fix integers $d\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$. Let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the
component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]]
with its componentwise inner product, let $Q_{j}^{(1)},P_{k}^{(1)}$ be the
scalar position and momentum operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]], and let
$\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with
$\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^{1}$
([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Write
$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}:=\Psi_{0}\bigl(\bigoplus_{l}\mathcal F_{2}\bigr)\Psi_{0}^{-1}$
for its componentwise version, with $\Psi_{0}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] clause (a).
Define, componentwise,
$$D(Q_{j}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (Q_{j}f)_{l}:=x_{j}f_{l},$$
$$D(P_{k}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ D_{k}f_{l}\text{ exists in }L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
where $D_{k}$ is the weak derivative of [[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]].
Write $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the classes whose components
lie in $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]),
and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the componentwise Schwartz
class ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]). Then:

(a) under $\Psi_{0}$ the operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are the orthogonal sums
$\bigoplus_{l}Q_{j}^{(1)}$ and $\bigoplus_{l}P_{k}^{(1)}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-orthogonal-sums-of-self-adjoint-operators]]; in particular
$Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are densely defined and self-adjoint with the displayed
domains;

(b) $\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}$ is unitary,
$$D(P_{k})=\bigl\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ \xi_{k}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\bigr\},$$
and for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
$$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}(P_{k}f)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_{k}\,\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f(\xi)\qquad\text{for almost every }\xi;$$

(c) the componentwise translation $T_{a}^{(r)}f:=f(\cdot-a)$, $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$,
is unitary, leaves $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
invariant, satisfies $D_{k}(T_{a}^{(r)}f)=T_{a}^{(r)}(D_{k}f)$ for
$f\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$$T_{a}^{(r)}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}Q_{j}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I,\qquad T_{a}^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}P_{k}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=P_{k};$$

(d) for every $f\in D(P_{j})$,
$$\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t\bigl(T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}f-f\bigr)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}f \qquad\text{in }H^{(r)},$$
so the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}$ has generator $-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}$ and
$$T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}=\exp\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tP_{j}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the exponential being the spectral-calculus flow of the self-adjoint operator
$P_{j}$.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$. If $A$ has no eigenvalues, every preparation has an atomless outcome law: each singleton has probability zero, while $\mathbb R$ remains the outcome space and the law is concentrated on $\sigma(A)$ as in clause (d). Zero singleton probability does not exclude real point values as realizations of this law; it supplies no normalized exact-value eigenstate. A finite-resolution record is read through its declared Borel bin, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

**(a) Adopted model and state space.** Adopt the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 for a declared particle of mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and internal factor
assigned as in the identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]). Put $r:=2s+1$ and take
as the model's one-particle state space the complex Hilbert space
$$H_{s}:=L^{2}\bigl(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}\bigr) =\Bigl\{f:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb C^{r}\ \text{measurable}:\ \int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx<\infty\Bigr\}\Big/\!\sim,$$
the quotient by equality almost everywhere, with inner product
$\langle f,g\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\sum_{l=1}^{r}f_{l}\overline{g_{l}}\,dx$
linear in the first argument ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).
Thus an element of $H_{s}$ is a class of functions, not a function, and
pointwise values of a state are not defined; the position density is read from
the class through the observables of clause (b) and the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Its dimension
in the conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)1
is $\ell^{-3/2}$ per component. P5 presents the same space as the completed
tensor product $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\widehat\otimes\mathbb C^{r}$
with the spin factor carrying the representation of P6; the unitary
identification of the two descriptions and the componentwise reading of
componentwise operators are those of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] and
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]. The orthonormal
basis $(e_{m})_{m=-s,\dots,s}$ of $\mathbb C^{r}$ is the basis fixed by P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii)).

**(b) Position and momentum.** The model's $j$-th position and $k$-th momentum
are the componentwise operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a): for
$f=(f_{l})$, restricted to the classes with $x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}$ respectively
with $D_{k}f_{l}\in L^{2}$ for all $l$,
$$(Q_{j}f)_{l}(x):=x_{j}f_{l}(x),\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
with $D_{k}$ the weak derivative and $\hbar$ the action constant of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. These are the scalar operators of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]] applied
componentwise. The model assigns to $(Q_{j},\mathrm m)$ and to
$(P_{k},\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})$ the status of assigned sharp observables in
the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
clause (a), with the units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
clause (d)4; both are densely defined and self-adjoint by
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a). On the
Schwartz core they satisfy the componentwise canonical commutation relations,
and they commute with the internal-factor operators of clause (c) in the sense
of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] clauses (a),(c).

**(c) Internal factor.** For $i\in\{1,2,3\}$ let $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ be the
self-adjoint endomorphisms of $\mathbb C^{r}$ of the spin assignment P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii),
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]), and let the model read
them on $H_{s}$ as the matrix actions
$$(S_{i}f)_{l}:=\hbar\sum_{m=1}^{r}(J_{i})_{lm}f_{m}\qquad(l=1,\dots,r),$$
that is, as the amplifications $I\otimes S_{i}$ under the tensor
identification of clause (a) ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]]
clause (d)). Their declared unit is the unit of action ([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
clause (d)4). The factor is internal bookkeeping: it is not a spatial
coordinate, not a rotating body and not a relativistic spinor, and the model
assigns no position or worldline to it.

**(d) Momentum-space representative.** With $U^{(s)}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] for $r=2s+1$, the
**momentum-space representative** of a preparation vector $\psi\in H_{s}$ is
$\psi_{p}:=U^{(s)}\psi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$; for a
Schwartz class $\psi$ it is the componentwise Fourier transform
$$(\psi_{p})_{l}(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-3/2}\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}\psi_{l}(x)\,dx,$$
and its dimension is $(\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})^{-3/2}$ per component
([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)2). By
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] clause (b), $P_{k}$ acts on the
momentum representative by multiplication by $p_{k}$; this is the model's
momentum reading and no measured momentum distribution is identified with
$|\psi_{p}|^{2}$ by this definition.

**(e) Frame reading.** The model's inertial frames are the global coordinate
charts of P5; frame changes are the Galilean transformations of P5, with
parameters and units as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. This
definition uses P5's frame class only. For translations by $a\in\mathbb R^3$ and boosts with parameter $u\in\mathbb R^3$, choose the componentwise representative convention
$$(T_a\psi)(x)=\psi(x-a),\qquad (B_u(t)\psi)(x)=\exp\!\left(\frac{i}{\hbar}\left(mu\cdot x-\tfrac12m|u|^2t\right)\right)\psi(x-ut).$$
Here $a$ is length-valued, $u$ velocity-valued and $t$ time-valued, so the phase is dimensionless. These formulas specify classes almost everywhere and are chosen model conventions. The covariance theorems of this page derive operator and outcome-law identities conditional on these choices; they do not derive the choice of representative convention itself. No Lorentz transformation law is claimed.

**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) record the readings of P1, P2, P5 and P6 in the
terminology of this page and fix the objects used by its theorems. They assert
no time evolution beyond what the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 assigns
([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]
clause (iv)), no preparation or apparatus model, no detection model and no
empirical result. Massless particles, relativistic matter, radiation, singular
or unbounded potentials and boundary or confined realizations are separate
model assumptions with their own domains and self-adjointness statements; none
is obtained from this definition.

Adopt the postulates P1 and P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable with outcome law $\mu^{A}$ in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and let $\rho$ be a preparation. Then:

(a) **Pure preparations.** Let $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ be the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$. Then the mean of the outcome law exists and equals $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, and the second moment exists and equals $\|A\psi\|^{2}$:
$$m(\psi)=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2},$$
both read in the powers of the declared unit $u_A$ of the observable. If $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, the variance is
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\psi)\bigr)^{2}d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}.$$

(b) **Variance and its hypotheses.** For every unit $\psi\in D(A)$ the variance exists and equals
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\psi}(A)=\|A\psi\|^{2}-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}=\bigl\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\bigr\|^{2}\ge0,$$
without any hypothesis beyond $\psi\in D(A)$; no appeal to a discrete eigenbasis is made.

(c) **Non-existence is possible.** The identities of (a) and (b) are conditional on membership of $\psi$ in the stated domains. If $\psi\notin D(|A|^{1/2})$ then $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\infty$, so the mean of the outcome law does not exist as a finite real number; the mean is finite exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then $\psi$ need not lie in $D(A)$. If $\psi\notin D(A)$ then the second moment $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ is infinite. In particular every preparation of the model is a unit ray or a density operator, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments automatically.

(d) **Mixtures.** Let $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ be a spectral expansion of a preparation, $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, $(u_n)$ orthonormal. In every weighted moment sum, zero-weight terms are defined to be zero before evaluating a component integral; equivalently, only positive-weight indices are summed. This applies also to component means that are undefined at zero-weight indices. Then the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite if and only if $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$, and then $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$. For the second moment, put $M_n:=\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,u_n}$, so $M_n=\|Au_n\|^{2}$ for $u_n\in D(A)$ and $M_n=+\infty$ otherwise; a zero weight contributes zero. Then $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_nM_n\in[0,\infty]$, and it is finite exactly when every $u_n$ of positive weight lies in $D(A)$ and $\sum_{n:w_n>0}w_n\|Au_n\|^{2}<\infty$. Thus componentwise domain membership alone does not guarantee a finite mixed-state second moment. Whenever the mixture has a finite absolute first moment, the identity of clause (b) of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] gives its mean as the absolutely convergent weighted average of the component means.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1 and P2 together with the mathematical moment results cited below; they assert no apparatus resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance and no empirical value. Whether a concrete preparation has a finite mean or variance for a concrete assigned observable is a question about the pair $(\rho,A)$ and the tested identification of the observable, not a consequence of the framework's postulates alone.

**(a) Setting.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the
observable and probability postulate P2 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned sharp observable with
declared unit $u_{A}$ and outcome law $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ in a preparation
$\rho$, in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b).

**(b) Preparation variance.** When the mean
$m(\rho):=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and the second
moment $\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ of the outcome
law are finite, the **preparation variance** of $(A,u_{A})$ in $\rho$ is
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A):=\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\rho)\bigr)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda),$$
read in the square $u_{A}^{2}$ of the declared unit, and the **preparation
spread** is $\Delta_{\rho}A:=\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A)^{1/2}\ge0$, read in
the unit $u_{A}$. When either quantity is not finite the variance and the
spread of the pair in $\rho$ are **not defined**; the definition does not
extend them by $+\infty$.

**(c) Values and hypotheses.** The variance and its hypotheses are exactly
those of the moment theorem: for a pure preparation of a unit vector
$\psi\in D(A)$ the spread is $\Delta_{\psi}A=\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\|$,
equal to $\bigl(\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}\bigr)^{1/2}$
when $\psi\in D(A^{2})$; for a preparation $\rho$ the identities and existence
criteria are those of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] and
[[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]]. In particular, for an orthonormal density expansion
$\rho=\sum_n w_nT_{u_n,u_n}$, the mean is finite exactly when
$$\sum_{n:w_n>0}w_n\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}(\lambda)<\infty,$$
by [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]] clause (d); zero-weight
indices are omitted before evaluating their component integrals. For a pure
unit vector the corresponding criterion is membership in $D(|A|^{1/2})$
by clause (b). Componentwise domain membership alone does not imply
convergence of the weighted sum, and finite moments are not automatic.

**(d) Products of spreads.** For two assigned sharp observables $(A,u_{A})$
and $(B,u_{B})$ in a common preparation $\rho$ in which both spreads are
defined, the product $\Delta_{\rho}A\,\Delta_{\rho}B$ is a nonnegative real
number read in the product unit $u_{A}u_{B}$; for a pure preparation of a unit
vector in $D(A)\cap D(B)$ it is
$\|(A-a)\psi\|\,\|(B-b)\psi\|$ with the real means $a=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$
and $b=\langle B\psi,\psi\rangle$.

**(e) Reading and scope.** The spread $\Delta_{\rho}A$ is a property of the
pair (preparation, assigned observable): it is the standard deviation of the
outcome law that P2 assigns. It is not an apparatus resolution, not a
measurement error and not a disturbance of the preparation; those are further
objects that require a declared instrument or apparatus model and are not
introduced here. Clause (b) makes no claim that a preparation realizes a
specific laboratory state, that a laboratory procedure measures $A$ with
resolution $u_{A}$, or that the spread is observed in any experiment; the
identification of an apparatus with the pair $(A,u_{A})$ is a tested
identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] fixes the units in which the
displays are read.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix integers $d\ge1$,
$r\ge1$ and $\hbar>0$, let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the
component-valued space with the componentwise position and momentum operators
$Q_{j},P_{k}$ of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]
clauses (a) and (b), with domains
$$D(Q_{j})=\{f=(f_{l}):\ x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\},\qquad D(P_{k})=\{f=(f_{l}):\ D_{k}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\},$$
and let $D_{k}$ denote the weak partial derivative
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]). Then:

(a) *Product rule.* If $f\in H^{(r)}$ has $x_{j}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
and $x_{j}D_{j}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ (the latter read
componentwise), then $x_{j}f$ lies in $D(P_{j})$ and
$$D_{j}(x_{j}f)=f+x_{j}D_{j}f;$$

(b) *The product domain.* $D(Q_{j}P_{j})=\{f\in D(P_{j}):\ x_{j}D_{j}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\}$
and $D(P_{j}Q_{j})=\{f\in D(Q_{j}):\ D_{j}(x_{j}f)\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\}$,
and their intersection is
$$D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})=\bigl\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ D_{j}f,\ x_{j}f,\ x_{j}D_{j}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\bigr\};$$

(c) *Commutator identity.* For every $f\in D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$,
$$(Q_{j}P_{j}-P_{j}Q_{j})f=i\hbar\,f;$$

(d) *Core.* The componentwise Schwartz class
$\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]])
is contained in $D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$, and (c) holds on it.

No identity of unbounded products is asserted outside $D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$;
in particular no identity is asserted on $D(P_{j})$ alone.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix integers $d\ge1$,
$r\ge1$ and $\hbar>0$, and let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
with the componentwise position and momentum operators $Q_{j},P_{j}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]. Let
$\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ with $\psi\ne0$ be a class and let
$D_{P}:=D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$ be the product domain characterized in
[[lem-nrqm-uncertainty-product-domain-commutator-identity]] clause (b). Then
there is a sequence $(\varphi_{n})_{n\ge1}\subseteq D_{P}$ with
$$\varphi_{n}\to\frac{\psi}{\|\psi\|},\qquad Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\to\frac{Q_{j}\psi}{\|\psi\|},\qquad P_{j}\varphi_{n}\to\frac{P_{j}\psi}{\|\psi\|},\qquad \|\varphi_{n}\|=1$$
in $H^{(r)}$. In particular, if $\psi$ is a unit vector, then
$\varphi_{n}\to\psi$, $Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\to Q_{j}\psi$ and
$P_{j}\varphi_{n}\to P_{j}\psi$ in norm, and consequently
$$\langle Q_{j}\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle\to\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \|Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\|\to\|Q_{j}\psi\|,\qquad \langle P_{j}\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle\to\langle P_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \|P_{j}\varphi_{n}\|\to\|P_{j}\psi\| .$$

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the observable and
probability postulate P2 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_{A})$ and $(B,u_{B})$ be assigned sharp
observables with outcome laws $\mu^{A},\mu^{B}$ and let
$\Delta_{\rho}A,\Delta_{\rho}B$ be their preparation spreads in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]]. Let $\psi$ be a unit vector.
Whenever $\psi\in D(A)\cap D(B)$, put
$$a:=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad b:=\langle B\psi,\psi\rangle.$$
Then:

(a) **Weak form.** If $\psi\in D(A)\cap D(B)$, then the means $a,b$ are real,
the spreads $\Delta_{\psi}A$ and $\Delta_{\psi}B$ are defined, both are read in
the units $u_{A}$ and $u_{B}$, and
$$\Delta_{\psi}A\,\Delta_{\psi}B\ge\bigl|\operatorname{Im}\langle A\psi,B\psi\rangle\bigr| .$$

(b) **Robertson form.** If in addition $\psi\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$, that is
$B\psi\in D(A)$ and $A\psi\in D(B)$, then the pairing
$\langle[A,B]\psi,\psi\rangle:=\langle AB\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle BA\psi,\psi\rangle$
is defined, is purely imaginary, and
$$\Delta_{\psi}A\,\Delta_{\psi}B\ge\tfrac12\bigl|\langle[A,B]\psi,\psi\rangle\bigr| ,$$
read in the product unit $u_{A}u_{B}$; moreover the anticommutator refinement
$$(\Delta_{\psi}A)^{2}(\Delta_{\psi}B)^{2}\ge\Bigl(\tfrac12\bigl\langle\{(A-a),(B-b)\}\psi,\psi\bigr\rangle\Bigr)^{2}+\tfrac14\bigl|\langle[A,B]\psi,\psi\rangle\bigr|^{2}$$
holds, with equality in the refined bound if and only if $(A-a)\psi$ and
$(B-b)\psi$ are linearly dependent.

(c) **Bounded observables.** If $A$ and $B$ are bounded everywhere-defined
self-adjoint operators, then clauses (a) and (b) hold for every unit
$\psi\in H$ with all hypotheses automatic ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]).

(d) **Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1
and P2 and the cited mathematics. They concern the spreads of the two outcome
laws in one preparation; they introduce no joint outcome law, no apparatus
resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance of the preparation, and no
time observable. In particular no energy-time inequality is asserted, and
clauses (a)-(c) do not claim that a laboratory procedure realizes either
observable or attains the bounds; whether a concrete preparation and apparatus
realize the pair $(A,u_{A})$ and produce the spread $\Delta_{\psi}A$ is a
tested identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.

For vectors $u,v$ in a real or complex inner product space,

$$|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\lVert u\rVert\lVert v\rVert.$$

Equality holds if and only if $u$ and $v$ are linearly dependent, including the case in which either vector is zero.

A **real Hilbert space** is a real inner-product space $H$ ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]) whose induced-length metric is complete in the sense of [[def-complete-metric-space]]: every Cauchy sequence in $H$ for the norm $\|v\|=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}$ ([[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]]) converges to a point of $H$. A **complex Hilbert space** is a complex inner-product space with the same completeness property, so that a Hilbert space is exactly a real or complex inner-product space that is a Banach space for its induced norm ([[def-banach-space]]).

**The completion convention is the Cauchy-sequence one.**
[[def-banach-space]] defines completeness by convergence of Cauchy sequences, and this page keeps that convention throughout. It is weaker than $\sigma$-completeness — the assertion that every decreasing sequence of nonempty closed subsets with diameters tending to zero has a nonempty intersection. The two agree in ZFC, but Blackadar, Farah and Karagila note that the closest-point theorem on a $\sigma$-complete inner-product space is provable in ZF, whereas the Cauchy-complete form used below consumes the Axiom of Countable Choice; nothing here silently imports the stronger notion.

derivations.claim: [Product-domain case] Let $\varphi$ be a unit vector in $D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$. By [F1] the operators $Q_{j},P_{j}$ are the model's assigned sharp observables with their maximal domains, so the preparation spreads and the Robertson relation of [F5] apply to them. By [F3], $(Q_{j}P_{j}-P_{j}Q_{j})\varphi=i\hbar\varphi$, so $\langle[Q_{j},P_{j}]\varphi,\varphi\rangle=i\hbar\|\varphi\|^{2}=i\hbar$. By [F5] the product of the preparation spreads of the two assigned observables satisfies $\Delta_{\varphi}Q_{j}\Delta_{\varphi}P_{j}\ge\tfrac12|i\hbar|=\hbar/2$.

[Approximation] Let $\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ be a unit vector and let $(\varphi_{n})$ be the approximating sequence of [F4]. For every $n$, $\varphi_{n}$ is a unit product-domain vector, so step 1.1 gives $\Delta_{\varphi_{n}}Q_{j}\Delta_{\varphi_{n}}P_{j}\ge\hbar/2$. By [F2] and [F4], $\Delta_{\varphi_{n}}Q_{j}^{2}=\|Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\|^{2}-\langle Q_{j}\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle^{2}\to\|Q_{j}\psi\|^{2}-\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}=\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}^{2}$, and the analogous identity holds for $P_{j}$ with the momentum limits of [F4]; taking square roots and products gives $\Delta_{\varphi_{n}}Q_{j}\Delta_{\varphi_{n}}P_{j}\to\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}$. Hence the limit satisfies $\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}\ge\hbar/2$, which is (a); and on the product domain the same computation together with [F3] is the derivation of (b).

[Exact imaginary part] Keep the notation of step 2.1 and put $a_{n}:=\langle Q_{j}\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle$, $b_{n}:=\langle P_{j}\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle$, $x_{n}:=(Q_{j}-a_{n})\varphi_{n}$, $y_{n}:=(P_{j}-b_{n})\varphi_{n}$. Since $\varphi_n$ lies in both product domains, symmetry of $Q_j$ and $P_j$ gives $\langle[Q_j,P_j]\varphi_n,\varphi_n\rangle=\langle P_j\varphi_n,Q_j\varphi_n\rangle-\langle Q_j\varphi_n,P_j\varphi_n\rangle=-2i\operatorname{Im}\langle Q_j\varphi_n,P_j\varphi_n\rangle$. The means $a_n,b_n$ are real by [F2], and expanding with the inner product linear in the first argument gives $\langle x_n,y_n\rangle=\langle Q_j\varphi_n,P_j\varphi_n\rangle-a_nb_n$; hence $\operatorname{Im}\langle Q_j\varphi_n,P_j\varphi_n\rangle=\operatorname{Im}\langle x_n,y_n\rangle$. By [F3], $\langle[Q_j,P_j]\varphi_n,\varphi_n\rangle=i\hbar$; hence $-2i\operatorname{Im}\langle x_n,y_n\rangle=i\hbar$ and $\operatorname{Im}\langle x_n,y_n\rangle=-\hbar/2$. By [F4], $x_{n}\to x$ and $y_{n}\to y$ in $H_{s}$ (each is the sum of a convergent term and a scalar multiple of a convergent term), so the inner product is continuous and $\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle=\lim_{n}\operatorname{Im}\langle x_{n},y_{n}\rangle=-\hbar/2$. This is the first display of (c).

[Equality characterization] For a unit $\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ put $\Delta_{Q}:=\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}$, $\Delta_{P}:=\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}$. By step 3.1, $\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle=-\hbar/2$, and by [F6] $$\hbar/2\le\Delta_{Q}\Delta_{P}=\|x\|\,\|y\|\ge|\langle x,y\rangle|\ge|\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle|=\hbar/2 .$$ Equality $\Delta_{Q}\Delta_{P}=\hbar/2$ holds exactly when both inequalities are equalities, that is (by the equality case of [F6] and the identity $|\langle x,y\rangle|^{2}=(\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle)^{2}+(\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle)^{2}$) when $x,y$ are linearly dependent and $\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle=0$. This completes (c).

[Scope] Clauses (a)-(c) were obtained from the model's operators, the product-rule identity, the approximation lemma and the Robertson relation; no joint outcome law, apparatus, disturbance, dynamics or empirical input enters. This is (d).
